title: Head and neck CT angiogram with labelled structures
summary: A CT angiogram of the head and neck from the TotalSegmentator CT dataset. The dataset's metadata lists the study type as CT angiography head and the pathology as none. It labels 48 structures within this volume, among them the brain, skull, cervical spine, thyroid gland and the carotid and subclavian arteries.

findings.text: The dataset's brain label covers this region of the head.

findings.text: The dataset's right common carotid artery label lies here.

findings.title: Aorta label
findings.text: The dataset's aorta label lies here, at the lower edge of this volume.

source.author: Jakob Wasserthal, University Hospital Basel (TotalSegmentator CT dataset)
source.attribution: TotalSegmentator CT dataset v3.0.0, case s0289. Wasserthal J, Department of Research and Analysis, University Hospital Basel. Zenodo, doi 10.5281/zenodo.22688904. Please cite Wasserthal J et al., TotalSegmentator: robust segmentation of 104 anatomical structures in CT images, Radiology: Artificial Intelligence 2023, doi 10.1148/ryai.230024.
source.modified: The lowest 16 slices of the source volume were cut off, which keeps the head, the neck and the upper chest down to the aortic arch. Converted to LPS voxel order. The per-structure masks were merged into one label volume and the 48 that are not empty after the cut are kept, with names written out in full. Where two masks overlapped (3,071 voxels in the source), the one later in alphabetical order won. CT values are unchanged. Stored as gzip chunks.

title: Brain MRI of an adult research participant
summary: A brain MRI of an adult research participant from the MPI Leipzig Mind-Brain-Body dataset. The dataset states no diagnosis for this participant. The series are a T1-weighted MP2RAGE image and a T2-weighted image. The dataset states that all anatomical images were defaced.

source.author: Babayan A, Baczkowski B and colleagues, MPI Leipzig Mind-Brain-Body dataset (OpenNeuro ds000221)
source.attribution: This data was obtained from the OpenfMRI database. Its accession number is ds000221. Babayan A, Baczkowski B, Cozatl R and colleagues (last author Villringer A), MPI-Leipzig Mind-Brain-Body, OpenNeuro, doi 10.18112/openneuro.ds000221.v1.0.0, participant sub-010003.
source.modified: T1w and T2w only, the FLAIR is not used. The T2w was resampled onto the T1w grid by linear interpolation using the headers of both files, which also removes a 1 degree tilt of the T2w. Converted to LPS voxel order and stored as whole-number int16 values. No other change. The defacing is the dataset's own.

title: Glioblastoma, four MRI sequences
summary: A brain MRI from the UPENN-GBM collection, whose collection page describes its patients as having de novo glioblastoma. There is no per-case diagnosis column. The collection's tumour masks are not part of the DICOM release, so this case has no labels and no findings. The sequences are T1, T1 post-contrast, T2 and FLAIR.

source.author: Bakas S, Sako C, Akbari H and colleagues, University of Pennsylvania Health System (UPENN-GBM)
source.attribution: Bakas, S., Sako, C., Akbari, H., Bilello, M., Sotiras, A., Shukla, G., Rudie, J. D., Flores Santamaria, N., Fathi Kazerooni, A., Pati, S., Rathore, S., Mamourian, E., Ha, S. M., Parker, W., Doshi, J., Baid, U., Bergman, M., Binder, Z. A., Verma, R., ... Davatzikos, C. (2021). Multi-parametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) scans for de novo Glioblastoma (GBM) patients from the University of Pennsylvania Health System (UPENN-GBM) (Version 2) [Data set]. The Cancer Imaging Archive. https://doi.org/10.7937/TCIA.709X-DN49. TCIA Data Usage Policy: https://www.cancerimagingarchive.net/data-usage-policies-and-restrictions/
source.modified: The CaPTk-processed T1, T1 post-contrast, T2 (a sagittal 3D acquisition) and FLAIR (3 mm slices) series were resampled onto the T1 grid by linear interpolation using the DICOM geometry, so the T2 and FLAIR are smoother across slices than they were acquired. Residual misregistration between series was measured at about 2 mm or less and not corrected. Converted to LPS voxel order. A box in front of the eyes and below the brow, the front 39 mm of the volume up to 85 mm above its bottom edge, was set to zero in all four series to remove the eyelid and nose contour left by the dataset's own face removal. No names, IDs or dates are kept.

title: Chest CT, COVID-19
summary: A chest CT from the COVID-CT-MD dataset. The dataset's clinical table lists the diagnosis for this patient as COVID-19. This patient has no slice or lobe labels in the dataset, so there are no findings.

source.author: Oikonomou A, Plataniotis K, Mohammadi A, Afshar P, Naderkhani F, Heidarian S and colleagues (COVID-CT-MD)

source.modified: Converted from DICOM to LPS voxel order. The in-plane size was reduced from 512 to 256 pixels by averaging 2 by 2 pixels. The slices are unchanged. Stored as gzip chunks. No header fields are kept.

title: Chest CT, lung adenocarcinoma
summary: A chest CT from the Lung-PET-CT-Dx collection. The collection states that patients whose code contains the letter A were diagnosed with adenocarcinoma, and this patient's code contains an A. The scan has three acquisitions of the same 46 slice positions at 5 mm, and this case shows the first. The collection says its annotation files indicate tumour location with bounding boxes, and seven annotated slices fall on this acquisition.

findings.title: Annotated tumour box
findings.text: The dataset's annotation for this patient is a bounding box around the tumour, and the box centre is marked here. The box is drawn on seven slices of this acquisition and this is the middle one. The marked mass lies in the left lung.

source.author: Li P, Wang S, Li T, Lu J, HuangFu Y, Wang D (Lung-PET-CT-Dx)
source.attribution: Li, P., Wang, S., Li, T., Lu, J., HuangFu, Y., & Wang, D. (2020). A Large-Scale CT and PET/CT Dataset for Lung Cancer Diagnosis (Lung-PET-CT-Dx) [Data set]. The Cancer Imaging Archive. https://doi.org/10.7937/TCIA.2020.NNC2-0461. TCIA Data Usage Policy: https://www.cancerimagingarchive.net/data-usage-policies-and-restrictions/
source.modified: Converted from DICOM to LPS voxel order and stored as gzip chunks. Only the first of the three acquisitions is kept. Pixel values are unchanged. No names, IDs, dates or other header fields are kept.

source.author: Masoudi M, Saadatmand-Tarzjan M, Ferdowsi University of Mashhad (FUMPE)
source.attribution: Masoudi, Mojtaba (2018). Patient34. figshare. Dataset. https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.6265679.v1. Part of Masoudi, Mojtaba; Saadatmand-Tarzjan, Mahdi (2018). FUMPE. figshare. Collection. https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.c.4107803.v1. Described in Masoudi M et al., Scientific Data 2018, doi 10.1038/sdata.2018.180.
source.modified: Converted from DICOM to LPS voxel order. The in-plane size was reduced from 512 to 256 pixels (2 by 2 averaging for the CT, nearest neighbour for the mask). Only the first 145 slices are kept, and the mask has no marked region above slice 140. The mask was reordered from the source MATLAB layout to match the CT, checked against the CT because the source does not state the order. Stored as gzip chunks. No header fields are kept.

title: Abdominal CT with pancreas and cancer labels
summary: A CT from the Medical Segmentation Decathlon pancreas task, whose description is pancreas and cancer segmentation. This case carries a pancreas label and a label named cancer. The dataset gives no diagnosis or report for the case.

findings.title: Pancreas and cancer labels

title: Liver CT, hepatocellular carcinoma
summary: A liver CT from the HCC-TACE-Seg collection, which holds patients with hepatocellular carcinoma. The series holds two acquisitions of the same slice positions, shown here as an earlier and a later series. The dataset's segmentation has four segments named Liver, Mass, Portal vein and Abdominal aorta, and it describes the Mass segment as Tumor. The collection's clinical table lists this patient's tumour as moderately differentiated and uninodular.

findings.title: Tumour segmentation
findings.text: The dataset's tumour segmentation lies here. The segment is named Mass and described as Tumor, and its outline is approximate, about 8 to 12 mm (3 to 5 slices) too high on the earlier acquisition and about 3 slices too low on the later one, so at the top and bottom of the mass the colour does not match the lesion and the mass should be judged from the image rather than from the colour. The mass is brighter than the liver around it on the earlier acquisition and darker on the later one.

findings.title: Liver segmentation
findings.text: The dataset's liver segment lies here. It leaves out the mass and the portal vein segments. At the dome of the liver it fits the later acquisition and runs into the lung on the earlier one.

findings.title: Portal vein segmentation
findings.text: The dataset's portal vein segment lies here. It is much brighter on the later acquisition than on the earlier one.

findings.title: Abdominal aorta segmentation
findings.text: The dataset's abdominal aorta segment lies here. It covers only a short stretch of 7 slices. The vessel is much brighter on the earlier acquisition than on the later one.

The DICOM segmentation was converted to a label volume on the same grid, reduced by nearest neighbour. No names, IDs, dates or other header fields are kept.

title: Lumbar spine MRI with vertebrae, discs and canal labelled
summary: Sagittal T1 and T2 lumbar spine MRI of patient 1 from the SPIDER dataset, which collects patients with a history of low back pain. The dataset labels the vertebrae, the intervertebral discs and the spinal canal. It gives per-level radiological gradings but no single diagnosis for this patient. Vertebrae and discs are numbered from the bottom, and the dataset says these numbers are not anatomical levels.

findings.title: Spinal canal, vertebra and disc labels
findings.text: The dataset's labels for the spinal canal, the vertebrae and the discs lie in this slice. The vertebrae and discs are numbered from the bottom.

findings.title: Lowest disc label
findings.text: The lowest disc label (label 201) lies here, below the lowest labelled vertebra.

source.modified: Converted from NIfTI to LPS voxel order after correcting the file's header. The header axes did not match the anatomy, so the voxel axes were assigned from the anatomy: along the file axes, anterior, superior and the patient's right. Float values were rounded to whole numbers and stored as int16, and the label is stored as uint8 on the same grid. Stored as gzip chunks.
